facts.statement: The extinct genus Plioperdix was described by Kretzoi in 1955.
Plioperdix is an extinct genus belonging to the family Phasianidae.
facts.quote: Plioperdix is an extinct genus of phasianid that lived during the Neogene period.

facts.statement: Plioperdix lived during the Neogene period.
facts.quote: Plioperdix is an extinct genus of phasianid that lived during the Neogene period.

facts.statement: Plioperdix lived between 8.725 and 5.09 million years ago, spanning the Tortonian to Zanclean ages.
facts.quote: Time range: Tortonian to Zanclean (8.725 to 5.09 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database classifies Plioperdix under the class Reptilia.
Plioperdix belongs to the parent group Phasianidae.
Plioperdix ponticus lived in Moldova and southern Ukraine during the Zanclean age.
facts.quote: Plioperdix ponticus inhabited Moldova and southern Ukraine during the Zanclean

facts.statement: Plioperdix ponticus was found in Transbaikalia and Mongolia during the Piacenzian age.
facts.quote: and Transbaikalia and Mongolia during the Piacenzian.

facts.statement: Plioperdix africana lived in Morocco during the Piacenzian age.
facts.quote: P. africana inhabited Morocco during the Piacenzian.

facts.statement: Plioperdix hungarica is known from the Late Miocene of Hungary and Russia.
facts.quote: P. hungarica is known from the Late Miocene of Hungary and Russia

facts.statement: It is debated whether Plioperdix hungarica is a valid species of Plioperdix.
facts.quote: though its validity as a species of Plioperdix has been questioned.
